title: Inference: scaling on queue depth, and what a cold start costs
purpose: Push load at one replica until its queue grows. The autoscaler must add a replica on that signal. Then measure where the time of that new replica went, with and without a warm node waiting.

steps.display: kubectl get nodes -l ds03/pool=inference   # before the test: one replica, one node
steps.output: 1 GPU node in the inference pool

steps.display: kubectl -n inference get scaledobject vllm-qwen   # the autoscaling signal: requests waiting in the model servers' queues
kubectl create -f loadgen-job.yaml   # lg-load-cold: 32 concurrent streams for 600 s through the gateway
kubectl -n inference get deploy,hpa   # the autoscaler added a replica
steps.output:
NAME                              READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
deployment.apps/qwen-router-epp   1/1     1            1           3h39m
deployment.apps/vllm-qwen         2/2     2            2           3h35m

NAME                                                     REFERENCE              TARGETS     MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
horizontalpodautoscaler.autoscaling/keda-hpa-vllm-qwen   Deployment/vllm-qwen   0/4 (avg)   1         2         2          10m

steps.display: Prometheus: max over the last 15 minutes of sum(vllm:num_requests_waiting)
cold start of the new replica (new GPU node bought for it)
kubectl -n gpu-buffer get pods -o wide   # the warm buffer: a low-priority pod holding a GPU node, serving image already pulled
steps.output:

gpu-buffer-78f5cd7cc9-87md4   1/1     Running   0          6m29s   10.31.19.19   i-02477228601a8b63c   <none>           <none>

steps.display: time to bring the buffer node up
kubectl create -f loadgen-job.yaml   # lg-load-warm: 32 concurrent streams for 600 s through the gateway
cold start of the new replica (warm buffer node)
kubectl -n gpu-buffer get events   # what happened to the placeholder
steps.output:
Killing: Stopping container hold
Preempted: Preempted by pod 1a17b0de-0302-4dfd-bc03-a98bbeaba9f3 on node i-02477228601a8b63c

checks.description: the autoscaler watches requests waiting, not CPU or GPU utilization
checks.because: GPU utilization is high at any load, so it says nothing about whether users wait; queue depth does.

checks.description: the queue grew, and the autoscaler added a second replica because of it
checks.because: With at most 8 sequences per replica and 32 concurrent streams, requests queue; KEDA reads that from Prometheus.

checks.description: the cold replica needed a new GPU node
checks.because: The pool held exactly one node, used by the first replica, so the second replica had to buy one.

checks.description: the load completed without errors while scaling out
the new replica took over the buffer's node
checks.because: The replica's pod has a higher priority class than the placeholder, so the scheduler evicted the placeholder to make room.

checks.description: a replica placed on a warm node starts at least 2 minutes sooner than one that needed a new node
checks.because: The warm path skips the node launch and the image pull: 504 s cold against 125 s warm.

checks.description: on the warm path the 10 GB serving image was not pulled again
checks.because: The placeholder pod used the same image, so the 10 GB serving image was already on the node. (The small image of the weight-fetching init container is separate.)
